title: Safety-equipment subsidy support for an agro processor in Hisar
challenge:
Hisar district, Haryana · Agro processing

Approximately ₹30 lakh in recorded new safety-equipment expenditure

Rapid supported an agro-processing unit's safety-equipment subsidy assignment by bringing the expenditure, assessment and site information into the application work.

A defined equipment investment

The recorded expenditure concerned new safety equipment. The advisory question was how that investment should be examined and documented for the relevant incentive application.

Approximately ₹30 lakh was recorded as taxable equipment value for assessment. This is an expenditure measure. It does not describe the plant's total value, company turnover or subsidy amount received.

The records behind the work

Rapid's assessment brought together the business activity, equipment expenditure, safety-related information and the unit's land and approval context.

Those records had different roles. The expenditure established the investment being discussed. The business and site information connected it to the applicant. The safety-related records explained the requirement around the equipment.

The work therefore involved more than presenting a single invoice or a general description of the unit.
solution:
What Rapid took forward

The job history records assessment, preparation of application documents, collection of signed copies and portal submission.

Rapid connected the equipment expenditure to the supporting unit information and carried the agreed application work through those stages. The assignment remained focused on the particular investment being claimed.
result:
The outcome

The client received safety-equipment subsidy support associated with the investment. Rapid's documented contribution was the assessment and application preparation supporting the claim.

A practical lesson for industrial investors

When an equipment purchase may have an incentive route, the application needs a clear account of the expenditure and the context around it. Keep the equipment value, the wider project budget and any eventual benefit separate.

This case shows how an investment made for a specific business requirement can be developed into a focused advisory assignment.

title: Capital-subsidy support for a manufacturing investment in Hisar
challenge:
Hisar district, Haryana · Manufacturing

Approximately ₹49 lakh in recorded machinery and building investment

Rapid brought the investment, production and site records together for a manufacturing unit's capital-subsidy assignment. The work connected a defined expenditure trail to assessment, application preparation and submission.

The investment behind the assignment

The unit had recorded expenditure across plant and machinery and its building. Together, those categories amounted to approximately ₹49 lakh.

For the subsidy work, a total investment figure was only the starting point. The application also needed to be understood through the unit's business constitution, production date and site records. Each part explained a different aspect of the investment.

The scale shown here refers to the recorded machinery and building expenditure. It is not a statement of company turnover, complete project value or subsidy received.
solution:
What Rapid took forward

Rapid's assessment brought the machinery and building figures together with the recorded commercial-production date, constitution and land-related information. That established the project context for the application work.

The assignment progressed through preparation of application documents, collection of signed copies and portal submission. It required coordination between the financial record of the investment and the unit's operating and site details.

A building cost, a machine cost and a land record are not interchangeable evidence. Keeping them distinct made the application about the actual project rather than a general claim that the business had invested money.
result:
The outcome

The client received capital-subsidy support associated with the manufacturing investment. Rapid's contribution covered the assessment and application work connecting the expenditure and project records to the claim.

What a similar business can take from this case

A useful subsidy assignment starts with a clear investment basis. Separate the categories, establish the dates and connect the spending to the unit making the application.

For a manufacturer planning an expansion, this is a reason to organise the new investment separately from the existing business. It gives the advisory work a defined project to examine and pursue.

title: Testing-equipment subsidy support for an agro processor in Sirsa
challenge:
Sirsa district, Haryana · Agro processing

Approximately ₹16.5 lakh in testing-equipment investment

An agro-processing business invested in an analyser used to test oil and moisture content in mustard seed. Rapid connected that equipment's purpose and expenditure records to a testing-equipment subsidy assignment.

A focused investment within a processing business

The assignment concerned a specific analyser, rather than the cost of an entire plant. Its testing purpose helped explain why the equipment had been purchased and how it related to the unit's activity.

The investment recorded for assessment was approximately ₹16.5 lakh. This figure describes equipment expenditure, not company turnover, subsidy value or an increase in operating performance.

Connecting the equipment to the application

Rapid's assessment captured the cost, purchase date, technical identity and intended use of the analyser. It also recorded the unit's location and land context.

Earlier assistance was another relevant question. The assessment recorded whether testing subsidy had been availed previously, so the new application could be examined with that history in view.

This mattered because a new purchase should be understood in its actual business and application context. The equipment description and invoice value alone did not answer every question.
solution:
The work Rapid handled

The job history records document collection, assessment, preparation of application documents, signed copies and portal submission.

Rapid brought those steps together around a defined claim: the applicant, the equipment, its testing function and the expenditure behind it. That gave the assignment a clear basis for preparation and follow-through.
result:
The outcome

The client received testing-equipment subsidy support associated with the investment. The case demonstrates Rapid's assessment and application work for a specific equipment-based incentive engagement.

What this means for a processing business

An incentive discussion does not always begin with a new factory. It can arise from a targeted equipment purchase within an established operation.

Describe what the equipment does, retain the purchase and payment records and identify any earlier assistance. Those details give the advisory team something concrete to examine.
